prompt:
Use case: product-mockup
Asset type: vertical repeating ribbon material for a wedding invitation navigation spine
Primary request: Create a tall narrow strip of the oxblood woven moiré silk ribbon seen in Image 1, isolated cleanly as a reusable material asset.
Input images: Image 1 is a palette, weave, stitch, and craft reference only; do not reproduce its numerals, botanical symbols, pins, seal, paper, lettering, or surrounding interface.
Scene/backdrop: no scene; orthographic top-down material sample running continuously from the top edge to the bottom edge.
Subject: one straight oxblood-black-cherry woven ribbon occupying the full canvas width, with clear longitudinal ribbing and large visible moiré waves, finished by two parallel rows of tiny antique-gold thread stitches close to each long edge.
Style/medium: photorealistic luxury grosgrain and moiré silk textile photography, tactile fiber detail, heirloom haberdashery craftsmanship.
Composition/framing: very tall portrait strip, minimum intended output 512 by 1536 pixels; ribbon continues exactly off the top and bottom for seamless-enough vertical stacking; perfectly straight long edges; no perspective, folds, knots, clips, or end caps.
Lighting/mood: even grazing studio light that makes ribbing, silk wave, and metallic thread obvious after downscaling; rich dark tonal range without crushed detail.
Color palette: oxblood #3C141C and black cherry with muted antique-champagne gold stitching, no bright yellow gold.
Materials/textures: pronounced woven ribs, moiré interference waves at large scale, fine double stitched edges with slight real thread irregularity.
Constraints: no transparency required; no text, no letters, no numbers, no symbols, no logo, no watermark, no seal, no pin, no paper, no people, no hands, no border outside the ribbon.
Avoid: satin bow, velvet, flat digital stripes, bright red, rope trim, chain, zipper, lace, paisley, repeating emblem, gradient-only treatment, CGI plastic fibers.
